title: The Vow of the Old Mill House
premise: Ines Almeida, a cellist whose hands failed her in a catastrophic final performance, retreats to the old mill house beside a struggling Portuguese vineyard, keeping love safely in the past tense. When Gabriel Reyes — the man behind ten years of anonymous letters she never answered — moves in next door to save his family's harvest from his corrupt uncle's land grab, Ines is pulled into the fight and forced back into the world of music she abandoned. As the first harvest approaches, Ines must choose between a career-saving comeback that would take her away forever and staying with the man who finally sees her whole. She chooses neither path as offered: she plays one defiant public concert at the harvest festival, reclaiming music on her own terms, while Gabriel wins the mill house and vineyard back, and they begin together with no vows but their own.
about_author: Jude Thornbury is the pen name of a former orchestral cellist who traded concert halls for a farmhouse in the Douro Valley, where she writes love stories among the vines. Her novels are known for wounded artists, stubborn families, and endings earned rather than given.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Three years after her hands betrayed her mid-concert, Ines unpacks her cello case at the old mill house without opening it. A neighbor brings bread and gossip about the vineyard's troubles. Beat: numb survival disguised as peace.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Answered
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Packing boxes reveal a decade of unsigned letters postmarked from the valley — tender, knowing, addressed to 'the girl who stopped playing.' She rereads them by firelight. Beat: longing she refuses to name resurfaces.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Gabriel Reyes moves into the neighboring quinta, recognizing Ines instantly though she doesn't know he wrote the letters. His uncle Duarte is pressuring him to sell. Beat: hope tangled with guilt over years of silence.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A first awkward meeting over a borrowed ladder; sharp banter masks recognition neither admits. Ines notices his hands — a musician's memory. Beat: wary curiosity cracking her isolation.

chapters.title: Duarte's Offer
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Uncle Duarte offers to forgive family debts if Gabriel sells and leaves Portugal for good, revealing forged papers claiming half the quinta. Gabriel refuses. Beat: the corruption takes shape; stakes become concrete.

chapters.title: The Vine That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Gabriel teaches Ines to read the vines before harvest; her fingers remember movement without pain for the first time. He almost tells her about the letters. Beat: tentative tenderness, fear of wanting again.

chapters.title: What the Town Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Village festival: Duarte publicly humiliates Gabriel over the debts, and Ines defends him instinctively. Whispers link Duarte to a developer. Beat: Ines realizes she's already inside this story.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confesses the catastrophe of her final performance — not injury but panic, then shame — and why she keeps love in the past tense. Gabriel listens without pity. Beat: raw honesty deepening intimacy.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Gabriel discovers Duarte's forged deed relies on a signature his dead father supposedly made — dated during a hospital stay. He photographs evidence. Beat: quiet fury; the fight becomes winnable.

chapters.title: First Touch
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Rain traps them in the mill house; Ines plays two bars on a borrowed guitar, laughing for the first time in years. They kiss. Beat: joy arriving like weather, uninvited and undeniable.

chapters.title: The Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Ines finds drafts of the letters in Gabriel's desk and confronts him — a decade of devotion he never claimed. Hurt that he watched her grieve from hiding. Beat: betrayal inside tenderness; first rupture.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Harvest begins; the whole village works the rows while Duarte's men survey the boundary lines. Ines and Gabriel work apart, aching. Beat: communal warmth against private cold.

chapters.title: The Comeback Call
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines's old manager arrives with an offer: a prestigious comeback tour, proof her career can be saved, leaving in three weeks. Beat: temptation wearing the face of rescue.

chapters.title: Duarte Tightens
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Duarte files an injunction freezing the quinta's assets before harvest sales, and threatens Ines's lease on the mill house to pressure Gabriel. Beat: power corrupting openly; love weaponized.

chapters.title: Two Weeks
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines rehearses for the tour and finds her hands steady only when playing for the village children, not for the audition video. She understands what the career was saving her from. Beat: clarity through contrast.

chapters.title: The Boundary Stone
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Gabriel and Ines find the original boundary stone moved years ago — physical proof of Duarte's fraud — but Duarte's foreman catches them and destroys the photograph. Beat: setback; allies needed.

chapters.title: The Village Rises
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ines rallies the villagers; the old priest produces church records matching the true stone's location. Duarte retaliates by revealing Gabriel's anonymous letters to humiliate him. Beat: solidarity against shame.

chapters.title: What I Was Saving
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On the eve of the hearing, Ines tells Gabriel she declined the tour — not for him, but because she wants music that means something. He asks her to play at the harvest festival. Beat: choice made; terror and resolve.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Gabriel's POV. Courtroom climax: the priest's records, a surviving photograph, and Duarte's own foreman testifying under oath break the forgery open. The quinta is saved. Beat: justice earned collectively.

chapters.title: Concerto for a Courtyard
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax: before the whole village at the harvest festival, Ines performs — hands trembling, then sure — her first public playing since the catastrophe. Gabriel watches from the front row. Beat: reclamation; the catastrophic night finally answered.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The grapes come in; Duarte, exposed and indebted, leaves the valley. Gabriel gives Ines the mill house deed — her name on it — asking nothing. Beat: belonging offered freely, not bargained.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Epilogue: spring planting. Ines teaches village children cello in the courtyard, writes Gabriel a letter at last, and answers it herself. No vows but their own. Beat: love moved into the present tense; home.
